Proposition
[Induced Metric on $T^n$]

1. ch2:2.23↗ def:product-metric ↗ def:induced-metric The metric on $T^n=(S^1)^n$ induced by its standard product embedding equals the product of the usual induced metrics on the factors $S^1\subseteq \mathbb R^2$. In the formalized case $n=2$, $T^2=S^1\times S^1$: is the round metric on $S^1\subseteq \mathbb C$, is their product metric, and identifies it with the metric induced by the $L^2$-embedding into $\mathbb R^4$.

For a strictly positive smooth $f:M_1\to \mathbb R^+$, define the warped form on $M_1\times M_2$ by \begin{equation} g_{(p_1,p_2)}((v_1,v_2),(w_1,w_2))=g_1|_{p_1}(v_1,w_1)+f(p_1)^2g_2|_{p_2}(v_2,w_2). \end{equation} Unless $f$ is constant, this is generally not a product metric.
